$comment: Positions for the golden test. Deliberately few and deliberately varied -- each one is a different way the feature encoding can be wrong. Moves are GTP coordinates, the same encoding katascope sends on the wire.

positions.name: empty-19x19
positions.why: Baseline. A symmetric position: a transposed board or a flipped axis still looks plausible here, but the policy must be symmetric, which nothing else checks.

positions.name: opening-4-moves
positions.why: Asymmetric corners. Catches a transposed board and an x/y swap in the coordinate conversion.

positions.name: handicap-4-setup-stones
positions.why: initialStones rather than moves, and White to play first. Catches a side-to-move error and setup stones being dropped.

positions.name: with-passes
positions.why: Passes must advance the move history without placing a stone. Catches history planes being built from the stone list instead of the move list. The pass is followed by a real move on purpose -- a trailing pass puts the position one pass from game end, where KataGo hides history by design (see pass-would-end-game).

positions.name: small-9x9
positions.why: A board size the trunk was probably not trained at most often, and a different plane_area. Catches hardcoded 19s.

positions.name: rectangular-13x9
positions.why: Non-square. Catches board_x/board_y being used interchangeably, which a square board can never reveal.

positions.name: pass-would-end-game
positions.why: A trailing pass, so a pass by the side to move would end the game. KataGo sets maxTurnsOfHistoryToInclude = 0 here on purpose, hiding the history from the net; KataGo's Python Features has no equivalent. Excluded from the tight comparison and covered by its own test.
